extracted.intended_audience: EPA rule writers, program/regulatory staff, Standards Coordinators, and OGC attorneys
extracted.subtask_short: EPA rulemaking NTTAA and IBR compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for EPA staff on complying with the National Technology Transfer and Advancement Act (NTTAA) when developing rules and on use of incorporation by reference (IBR) to include external standards in Federal Register and CFR rule text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a voluntary consensus standard (VCS)
rubrics_metrics.description: A "voluntary consensus standard" is a technical standard developed or adopted by a legitimate standards-developing organization ("voluntary consensus standards body"). The Act defines "technical standards" as "performance-based or design-specific technical specifications and related management systems practices." According to NTTAA’s legislative history, a "technical standard" pertains to "products and processes, such as the size, strength, or technical performance of a product, process or material."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine whether a given standard qualifies as a VCS for purposes of NTTAA obligations; applies when a rule establishes or modifies technical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of a legitimate standards-developing organization
rubrics_metrics.description: A legitimate standards-developing organization must produce standards by consensus and observe the principles of due process, openness, and balance of interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ANSI evaluation/certification of a standards body is an important indicator that the body meets these criteria; EPA staff may seek OGC advice when making determinations and drafting the rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: When NTTAA obligations apply to a rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If your rule establishes a technical standard (e.g., a special method for collecting a water sample, or a new field or laboratory procedure for measuring a chemical parameter), it is very likely that there are existing VCS's that you will need to consider in the development of the regulation. If your rule does not involve the establishment or modification of technical standards, you have neither an obligation to address the rulemaking requirements of NTTAA nor to discuss the matter in the preamble to your rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule writers should seek out and consider any and all potentially-applicable VCS's, domestic or international, that might be used to carry out some or all of the rule's objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common types of VCSs relevant to EPA
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of EPA, the most common, potentially useful VCS's include field and laboratory test methods, sampling protocols and material specifications. Depending on the subject of your rule, other less likely types could apply (e.g., quality and environmental management systems, business practices, definitional standards and installation safety codes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be attentive to domain-specific standards beyond the common types when scoping a rule; consider both domestic and international standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find potential VCSs
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources include: the National Standards System Network (NSSN) maintained by ANSI (http://www.nssn.org), the National Center for Standards and Certification Information (NIST telephone service), your program office’s Standards Coordinator, and public comment during stakeholder outreach and notice-and-comment phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NSSN for broad searches (250,000+ standards indexed); contact NIST library service for free research; consult program Standards Coordinators for additional leads; solicit public input on potentially-applicable VCSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to address NTTAA in ANPRMs and NPRMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a brief discussion of NTTAA and its rule-related requirements in the rule’s preamble; solicit public comment on the use of VCS's in ANPRMs and NPRMs; if you have identified a VCS for possible inclusion, identify the VCS and explain why EPA is considering using it and request comment; if initially deciding not to propose the use of an existing VCS, explain your reasoning and request comment; request comments from the public on the existence of VCS's that should be considered for inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit and transparent about tentative positions to invite meaningful public input; identify standards early when possible to focus comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: NTTAA requirements for final rules (preamble content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a brief discussion of NTTAA and its rule-related requirements in the rule’s preamble; describe your efforts to find potential VCS's (specifically mention any outreach activities conducted with voluntary consensus standards bodies); if you elect to use an existing VCS, identify the VCS and any alternatives considered and explain the decision; if you elect not to use an existing potentially-applicable VCS, identify the VCS and explain how use would be inconsistent with applicable law or otherwise impractical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is in addition to the basic rulemaking requirement that EPA provide an appropriate explanation for its regulatory decisions; the summary explanation must also appear in the NTTAA Section of the preamble and the response-to-comments material in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of NTTAA discussion in the preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: In your NPRM and FRM, include any detailed NTTAA discussions in a separate section in an appropriate location within the 'Supplementary Information' section of the preamble. Include summary information at the end of the preamble, in a section titled 'National Technology Transfer and Advancement Act', along with the other Regulatory Assessment Requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary statements will be extracted for inclusion in the annual report that OMB is required to send to Congress; Agency work group is developing template language for this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to reference adopted VCSs in rule documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If a VCS was suggested by comment, address it in your response to comments section of the preamble and your response to comments document in the docket. A summary explanation must also be in the NTTAA Section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not quote the full text of a VCS in the rule text; incorporation by reference is normally required to make the VCS text binding in the rule (see IBR requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory mandate to use voluntary consensus standards (NTTAA §12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraph (3) of this subsection, all Federal agencies and departments shall use technical standards that are developed or adopted by voluntary consensus standards bodies, using such technical standards as a means to carry out policy objectives or activities determined by the agencies and departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must consult with voluntary private-sector consensus standards bodies and shall, when such participation is in the public interest and compatible with agency missions and resources, participate in standards development. If compliance is inconsistent with law or impractical, the agency head must transmit an explanation to OMB for inclusion in an annual report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory definition of technical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: As used in this subsection, the term 'technical standards' means performance-based or design-specific technical specifications and related management systems practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory definition governs whether a rule triggers NTTAA obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: IBR: purpose and limits (concept of incorporation by reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: IBR is a mechanism for applying to the regulated community, as a binding legal requirement, material an agency chooses not to publish verbatim in the Federal Register. APA 5 U.S.C. §552(a)(1) allows matter reasonably available to the affected public to be deemed published in the FR when incorporated by reference with approval of the Director of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IBR is narrower in purpose than placing material in the docket; Director approval is required and guided by whether material is 'reasonably available' and other criteria in 1 CFR Part 51.

rubrics_metrics.name: IBR eligibility criteria (material eligible for incorporation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Material is eligible for incorporation if it: • Is published data, criteria, standards, specifications, techniques, illustrations, or similar material; • Is reasonably available to and usable by the class of persons affected by the publication; • Does not reduce the usefulness of the Federal Register publication system; • Benefits the Federal Government and members of affected classes; and • Substantially reduces the volume of material published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the criteria the Director of the Federal Register applies when reviewing an agency's IBR request (1 CFR Part 51).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's presumption against agency-produced materials for IBR
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director 'will assume that a publication produced by the same agency that is seeking its approval is inappropriate for incorporation by reference.' While approval may be granted if the material meets basic requirements and 'possesses other unique or highly unusual qualities,' OFR does not typically approve such requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect that IBR will generally be approved for independently published materials (e.g., test methods by independent scientific organizations) or state-generated documents (e.g., SIP submittals), not agency-authored material that could be printed in FR/CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on using previously-published FR or U.S. Code material as IBR
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has determined that materials previously published in the Federal Register or in the United States Code are not appropriate for use as IBR. However, new Agency documents can include materials the Agency previously published in the CFR through the use of a cross-reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to incorporate by reference material already published in FR or U.S. Code; use cross-references where appropriate for CFR content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of statements of incorporation by reference in regulatory text
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements of incorporation by reference in regulatory text must: • Include the words 'incorporation by reference'; • Identify the standard and/or material to be incorporated, including the title, date, editing, author, and identification number of the publication; • Contain a statement of availability stating where and how copies may be obtained and examined; and • Refer to 5 U.S.C. 552(a) or include an approval statement that the Director of the Federal Register approves the incorporation by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use OFR-provided guidance language in the Document Drafting Handbook (examples provided) to ensure titles and numbers are identified completely and specifically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble placement and content requirements for IBR
rubrics_metrics.description: The preamble in the final rule document must reference the IBR in two locations: 1) The DATES caption must include an approval statement that indicates the effective date of the incorporation by reference as approved by the Director of the Federal Register. 2) The List of Subjects in the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION must include the term 'incorporation by reference.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure both locations are present in the final rule preamble to reflect OFR approval and effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: OFR submission package contents and timing for IBR approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agency must submit a written request for IBR approval to the Director of the Federal Register. The request must be submitted no less than 20 working days before the final rule document is submitted to OFR for publication. OFR will not consider any package that does not include: 1) A letter requesting approval of the incorporation; 2) A copy of the material to be incorporated; and 3) A copy of the final rule document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early submission is encouraged; an unsigned copy of the rule may be included to secure approval prior to signature. OFR will notify the Agency of approval or disapproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality, completeness, and organization requirements for materials forwarded to OFR
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials forwarded to OFR must be legible, complete, and contain identifying data including the title, date, author, publisher, and identification number of the publication. The OFR stresses that IBR material must be legible (not too light or blurred), complete (no text cut off), and that EPA must submit an official version of the material. Titles and numbers referencing the IBR material in the rule text must be identified completely and specifically. Material should be organized (preferably in a binder with tabs) in the same order as set out in the rule language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Package IBR materials carefully; include title pages or official documents identifying the official version to facilitate OFR review and timely publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum Federal Register publication requirements for proposed rules (APA §553(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum Federal Register Publication Requirements for Proposed Rules: Statement of the time, place, and nature of public rulemaking proceedings; Reference to the legal authority under which the rule is proposed; Either the text of the proposal, substance of the proposal, or description of subjects and issues involved; Description of who may be affected by the regulation; Description of any additional information relevant to the rulemaking but not included in the FR notice, and how to obtain it; Identification of provisions that may be changed in the final rule, solicitation of comment on controversial provisions and how to submit comments; Description of regulatory requirements imposed by other statutes, such as the Paperwork Reduction Act and the Regulatory Flexibility Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information on which the Agency relies and the methodology used must be exposed to public view but may be placed in the public docket rather than published in the FR, so long as it is easily accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes of the notice of proposed rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Under applicable case law, the notice of proposed rulemaking serves three purposes: • improve quality of rulemaking by exposing proposed regulations to diverse public comment; • provide opportunity to be heard and participate meaningfully in rulemaking process; and • enhance quality of judicial review by giving parties an opportunity to develop evidence in the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft NPRMs to meaningfully enable these purposes — provide sufficient factual and methodological detail either in the notice or readily accessible docket material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum Federal Register publication requirements for final rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum Federal Register Publication Requirements for Final Rule: Text of the rule; Description of statement of basis and purpose and where it is available; Description of response to comments document and where it is available; Description of document discussing major changes from proposal and where it is available; Description of regulatory requirements imposed by other statutes, such as the Paperwork Reduction Act and the Regulatory Flexibility Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Like proposed notices, final notices must contain minimum information in FR or make it easily accessible in a public docket; CAA §307(d) and other statutes impose additional specific documentary requirements for certain rulemakings.
